author: derekchiang
content: could you clarify why 2MB blocks are expected today under congestion?  do you mean that L2s would fall back to posting calldata if blobs are congested?  and by "break contracts with the repricing" you are talking about contracts that hardcode gas values similar to what's going on with 8037?  but didn't we align that hardcoding gas values is an anti-pattern that we shouldn't support?

author: derekchiang
content:
this is a good prompt -- i did not realize that we already benchmarked 2MB payloads in the context of nonPQ.  so to be clear in my simulation, the bar i used was for home nodes to receive the payload before 6s, but upon reflection that's probably an unnecessarily high bar because it probably doesn't matter much if home nodes can't make the PTC votes

so i reran the simulation with 4s reveal, and this time with a bar of 9s instead of 6s (giving home nodes 3s to execute the payload so they can follow the chain), and this time even 2MB payloads were able to propagate through the network.  so my earlier conclusion that PQ payloads can't propagate under today's network was wrong if we are OK with home nodes missing PTC duties.  though of course if we do 8411 or similar we'd be able to support TPS higher than today's, and more home nodes would be able to participate in PTC duty

to be clear this is separate from the question about whether we need to bump 7870 bandwidth requirements -- we might still need to bump it because PQ-Gasper puts a lot of bandwidth pressure on nodes, as my/kamil/Nashatyrev's simulations showed

author: potuz
content: Not that fancy: at the 200MGas target of Gloas with the new pricing, a full block with the typical transactions would be that large. The worst block can be much larger. But a typical full block will be about 2MB. And we see many of them. Now change signatures to Sphincs. And think not only in each transaction but think how apps like cowswap will pack signed messages and we will get much larger blocks I assume

author: potuz
content: As for contracts breaking that's also much simpler: today contracts require some transactions that, under the new pricing will be just more than 60Mgas. So we MUST increase the gas limit if we change the pricing or those apps simply don't work anymore. In principle they should be fine cause even though they'll be paying more gas. Gas will be cheaper. But if we change pricing and we don't increase the gas limit because of PQ, that's the worst possible scenarios for these apps

author: kevaundray
content: How is this possible given EIP-7825?

author: potuz
content: That EIP just caps per tx  gas limit, not the number of txs, if the block gas limit is high and it's full, the block size plus it's bal can be very large at 200M

author: kevaundray
content: Right, I was more saying that a contract shouldn’t require/expect a tx to be anywhere near 60Mgas

author: potuz
content: Ah sure, but still contracts whose txs are expensive now can get much more expensive in gas units in Gloss. I was under the impression that the limit in 7825 was chosen already accounting for these contacts not to break
